# Brake fluid flush and bleeding

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Locate the ABS connector, drain old fluid, fill with new DOT 3 brake fluid, bleed wheels until clear, then repeat for the clutch. [t988]

## Tools

- 10mm box end wrench [t988]
- [Partial] 8mm box end wrench (manual only) [t988]
- 3/8 inch ID clear tubing [t988]
- [Partial] Turkey baster [t988]
- [Partial] Catch container [t988]
- [Partial] 8mm box end wrench [t988]

## Parts

- [Partial] New DOT 3 brake fluid [t988]
- [Partial] RTV Silicone Sealant [t988]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use a turkey baster with the tip opened to fit about 4 inches of clear tubing into the reservoir bottom. [t988]
- Keep an eye on the reservoir level throughout flushing so it does not completely empty and suck in air. [t988]
- Watch for the clutch paddle to return when releasing the bleeder before locking it back on. [t988]
- Continue until clean, clear fluid comes out of the line. [t988]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Allowing the reservoir to run dry and sucking in air during the flush. [t988]
- [Partial] Breaking a seized bleeder by rushing without cleaning or penetrating oil first. [t988]
